name: Rotate and repair Ingress TLS
objective: CKS › Cluster Setup. Drill EVERY corner of terminating TLS at the Ingress harder than the exam: build a kubernetes.io/tls Secret from a self-signed cert, wire a spec.tls block, pin the backend rule, bind an ingressClassName, keep tls hosts aligned with rule hosts, rotate the cert in place under the same name, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix on a broken Ingress. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Rotate the certificate in place
questions.teach:
Because the Ingress references the Secret **by name**, you rotate a cert without touching the Ingress: replace `web-tls`'s contents under the **same name**. The clean idiom is `kubectl create secret tls web-tls --cert=... --key=... --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`.

**Gotcha:** don't rename the Secret during rotation — a new name breaks the Ingress link and the controller falls back to plain HTTP.
questions.prompt:
The seeded `web-tls` currently holds a stale cert whose subject CN is `old.example.com`. Rotate it: generate a NEW self-signed cert+key for CN `demo.example.com` and replace the Secret under the same name `web-tls`, leaving the Ingress reference intact.

Target: Secret `web-tls` is still `kubernetes.io/tls` with tls.crt+tls.key, its cert CN is now `demo.example.com` (not `old.example.com`), and Ingress `web` still references it in spec.tls.
questions.hint: Regenerate with openssl (`-subj "/CN=demo.example.com"`), then `kubectl -n ingress-learn create secret tls web-tls --cert=tls.crt --key=tls.key --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`. Do NOT edit the Ingress.
questions.solution:
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout tls.key -out tls.crt -days 365 -subj "/CN=demo.example.com"
kubectl -n ingress-learn create secret tls web-tls --cert=tls.crt --key=tls.key --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n ingress-learn get ingress web -o jsonpath='{.spec.tls[*].secretName}'   # web-tls

verification.description: web-tls rotated to CN demo.example.com (still kubernetes.io/tls) and Ingress web still references it

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: an Ingress not terminating TLS
questions.teach:
When an HTTPS host serves the wrong (default) cert or plain HTTP, inspect the Ingress with `kubectl get ingress <n> -o yaml` and check that `spec.tls.secretName` names an **existing** Secret and that the tls `hosts` match the rule host. A `secretName` pointing at a non-existent Secret means no cert is loaded.

**Gotcha:** fix the Ingress to reference the Secret that actually exists — don't invent a new Secret name.
questions.prompt:
Ingress `shop` in `ingress-learn` should terminate TLS for host `shop.example.com` using the existing Secret `shop-tls`, but it's broken: its `spec.tls` references the wrong secret name and so no cert loads. Diagnose and fix it. Don't delete and rebuild from scratch — find and fix what's wrong.

Target: Ingress `shop` has a `spec.tls` entry with `secretName=shop-tls` covering host `shop.example.com`, and a rule routing `shop.example.com` to Service `web`:80.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n ingress-learn get ingress shop -o yaml` — the `spec.tls[*].secretName` doesn't match the real Secret. List Secrets (`kubectl -n ingress-learn get secret`); the TLS one is `shop-tls`. Patch the Ingress to reference it.
questions.solution:
# describe/get shows spec.tls.secretName points at a Secret that doesn't exist; the real one is shop-tls
kubectl -n ingress-learn patch ingress shop --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/tls/0/secretName","value":"shop-tls"}]'
kubectl -n ingress-learn get ingress shop -o jsonpath='{.spec.tls[*].secretName}'   # shop-tls

verification.description: Ingress shop: spec.tls secretName shop-tls covers shop.example.com, rule routes to web:80
